title: AI history dataset: 106 scored and sourced events (1943 to 2026)
description:
106 milestones in the history of artificial intelligence from 1943 to 2026, each dated, categorized, scored for significance under a published rubric and linked to its primary source.

Curated by Chronicle, an interactive, sourced timeline of AI history. Every row links to a full dossier with the evidence behind it. This record archives the snapshot of 2026-10-24; the current version, with CSV and JSON downloads, is at epoch.founden.co/data.

Fields:

  • id (string): Stable identifier of the event, also its dossier slug.
  • date (string): When it happened: YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY when only the year is established.
  • year (integer): Calendar year.
  • date_precision (string): day, month or year: how precisely the date is known.
  • name (string): The subject as people name and search for it, for example Turing test.
  • title (string): Editorial headline.
  • organization (string): The person, lab or institution behind it.
  • category (string): Models, Research, Launches, Open source, Benchmarks, Policy, Culture or Robotics.
  • summary (string): What happened, in one sentence.
  • impact (string): Why it mattered, in one sentence.
  • significance_score (integer): Editorial significance from 0 to 100: the weighted sum of the 5 ratings under rubric 1.0.
  • tier (string): Defining (80 to 100), Major (60 to 79) or Notable (0 to 59).
  • confidence (string): Established, Supported or Provisional: how settled the evidence and historical perspective are. It does not change the score.
  • rating_novelty (integer): Conceptual shift, 0 to 5, worth 30% of the score: How much did this change the available approach?
  • rating_influence (integer): Downstream influence, 0 to 5, worth 25% of the score: How much subsequent research or practice does it underpin?
  • rating_reach (integer): Breadth of impact, 0 to 5, worth 20% of the score: How widely did the change matter beyond its original setting?
  • rating_access (integer): Access & diffusion, 0 to 5, worth 15% of the score: How much did it enable others to use or build on the work?
  • rating_institutions (integer): Institutional change, 0 to 5, worth 10% of the score: Did it change lasting infrastructure, governance, or incentives?
  • primary_source_url (string): The original paper, announcement or archive record.
  • source_count (integer): Sources cited in the event's dossier.
  • dossier_url (string): The event's full, cited dossier.

How events are chosen and scored. Inclusion favors documented conceptual advances, enabling datasets and infrastructure, influential systems, material changes in access, and institutional turning points. A model release alone does not establish a breakthrough, and the coverage is curated rather than exhaustive. Each event is rated 0 to 5 on 5 criteria with explicit anchors: conceptual shift (30%), downstream influence (25%), breadth of impact (20%), access & diffusion (15%), institutional change (10%). The weighted sum is the 0 to 100 significance_score (rubric 1.0). Confidence is reported separately and never multiplies the score. Full rubric, anchors and limitations: methodology.

Curation and limitations. Events were selected, dated and rated through Chronicle's editorial process, with AI-assisted research and writing. Every event links an original source (a paper, an official announcement or an archive record), and the dossiers cite more. Scores are comparative editorial judgments, not measurements: they carry hindsight, English-language, availability and recency bias, and a score of 81 is not meaningfully more precise than 80. Recent events are marked Provisional. Corrections are welcome through the contact options on the site.
